look_here_first: Inspect the fingerlike flowering branches and paired spikelets. At the blade/sheath junction, find a membranous ligule. Southern versus large crabgrass requires a hand lens: lateral veins on the sterile lemma are usually smooth or only sparsely prickly in D. ciliaris, but noticeably roughened in D. sanguinalis.

best_field_traits: Spreading annual grass with fingerlike terminal flowering branches.
Spikelets usually paired along the flowering branch.
Membranous ligule at the leaf collar.
Sterile lemma lateral veins smooth or sparsely prickly under magnification.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Large crabgrass (D. sanguinalis) has more prickles on the sterile lemma lateral veins, often with hairier upper leaves. Smooth crabgrass (D. ischaemum) usually has smaller spikelets. Goosegrass (Eleusine indica) has a flattened whitish crown and dense, zipperlike rows of spikelets.
